Cauchy and amplitude equality force constant modulus and a common squared phase, hence scalar signs. Fiberwise equality exactly requires F2-affinity on each affine K-line. Finite differences in coordinates show mixed pair differences balanced over K by trace duality; mixed triples vanish since Tr(γabc λ³) cannot be additive for all a,b,c,λ when |K|>=4; hence only the constant, r linear trace terms and C(r,2) pairwise trace products remain, uniquely. Projective quotient removes global sign. Independently constructed binary line-affinity matrices: (m,d)=(4,2) nullity7, (6,3) nullity10, (8,2) nullity21, agreeing with 1+d*C(r+1,2). These finite checks corroborate but do not replace uniform proof; d=1 deliberately excluded.

originality.rationale: The exact final extremizer census is a mathematically immediate corollary of TWO established results: a published Gold-graph theorem proves the same NECESSARY-AND-SUFFICIENT line-affine phase classification for all m,k; Guo–Kopparty–Sudan (2012) Proposition 2.6 (and Props 2.2–2.3) completely determine the degree set and exact dimension of ANY lifted affine-invariant code. The base binary affine code on F_{2^d} has degree set {0,2^j : 0<=j<d}; lifting to K^r permits exactly the constant, degree 2^j in one coordinate, and degree (2^j,2^j) across two coordinates; forbidden bit-shadow sums exclude other monomials. This is 1+d[r+C(r,2)] independent binary dimensions, hence 2^{d*C(r+1,2)} projective lines. In particular a separately published Gold fifth-power (d=2) theorem explicitly gives all quadratic phases and precisely 2^{r²+r} projective classes. Exact theorem wording absent from earlier paper does not establish originality when the quantified claim follows from its stronger code structure plus known equality characterization.
